block.title: Nixpkgs clang 23 builds and boots SerenityOS
block.p: Upstream clang gained a SerenityOS driver in LLVM 23, so Serenity no longer needs its own patched compiler to be cross-compiled. Nixpkgs 26.11 has clang 23.1.3 in the binary cache. A script builds only the Serenity target's runtimes on top of it: compiler-rt from 23.1.3, and libunwind, libc++abi and libc++ from the LLVM commit Serenity pins, with Serenity's libc++ patch. That takes about a minute, against a whole LLVM build for Serenity's own toolchain script.

claim.p: With that toolchain, Serenity at 1a00c247 builds all 6,076 targets, kernel included, without a failure. Its disk image boots headless in QEMU without KVM, and runs Shell, LibJS and two AK test programs before it shuts itself down. libpizlo's Serenity core, linked against that build's libc.so, is missing only the 313 syscall natives the Serenity backend has to provide.

block.p: Fil-C's clang is LLVM 20 and has no Serenity target. Rebasing Fil-C onto LLVM 23 would bring the driver along; until then the upstream driver commit would need a backport.
